issue_context.title: roachtest: using custom AdminUIPort breaks automated prometheus scraping
issue_context.body:
Per [1], in order to support multiple tenants on the same host, a unique, custom SQLPort is assigned (instead of `DefaultSQLPort`), similarly for `DefaultAdminUIPort`. The latter breaks current integration with Prometheus' service discovery which is configured to scrape on `DefaultAdminUIPort` (26258). Per [2], some tests revert to it via an explicit call to `SetDefaultAdminUIPort`. Otherwise, a custom AdminUIPort is used, in which case the metrics no longer show up in Grafana. Thus, a number of roachtest failures are now without metrics; e.g., grafana link in [3] yields no data.

[1] https://github.com/cockroachdb/cockroach/issues/111052
[2] https://github.com/cockroachdb/cockroach/pull/114097
[3] https://github.com/cockroachdb/cockroach/issues/116992

Jira issue: CRDB-34993

review_comments: Note that this won't work in the context of the `update-targets` roachprod command: in that case, we'll need to add the `--insecure` option to the command and pass that option when instantiating the cluster (see `startCmd` as an example).

Could you explain to me how prom knows to make an insecure request based off of this? I see in the [prom helper](https://github.com/cockroachlabs/prom-helper-service/blob/db9f7ccb5fac0d681abb61aa956e56509e68ae96/handlers/instanceconfigs/put.go#L68-L71), we append insecure to the config file name:

```
	if r.Insecure {
		configDirSuffix = inSecureConfigDirSuffix
	}
	fileName := fmt.Sprintf("%s%s/%s.%s", instanceConfigDir, configDirSuffix,
```

Is that all prom needs to know? It doesn't look like we do anything else with `r.Insecure`.
That is correct @DarrylWong . There are  locations where the target files are created: `cluster-configs` and `cluster-configs-insecure`

Ahh, and then prom has two different jobs based on the directory? That makes sense, although a tiny nit would be to maybe leave a one line comment explaining that. Otherwise you'd have to dig through the prometheus.yml file to find that info.
THanks @DarrylWong ! I added the comment in the promhelpers repo.
